description: Each asset belongs permanently to one of two latent types, and each type's next-period return follows an AR(1) in the asset's own last return: r_{t+1} = c_k + phi_k * r_t + sig_k * e. Reversal type: phi = -0.418, c = 0.00050, sig = 0.0139. Momentum type: phi = +0.419, c = 0.00044, sig = 0.0142. These are final estimates on explore + confirmation (450 assets), fitted after the confirmation test. The explore-only fit gave phi = -0.411 / +0.403, and an independent refit on confirmation gave -0.430 / +0.446. The intercepts do not differ between types (explore LR p = 0.88). Innovation sd is similar across types but varies continuously and persistently across assets; this volatility heterogeneity is a nuisance, not a third dynamic type (standardized K=3 vs K=2: dBIC = -9.1 explore, -12.0 confirmation). Type membership depends on age: P(momentum) = logistic(0.223 + 1.419 * age). About 54% of assets are momentum-type. Confirmation: the frozen explore gate predicts the history-inferred type with AUC 0.75; age logit coefficient 1.41, p = 1.9e-7. Lags beyond 1 add nothing once type is known; the pooled lag-2 coefficient of 0.176 is a mixture artefact (approximately E[phi^2]). No mean-return effect of size, liquidity, value, age or sector was confirmed (sector ANOVA on confirmation p = 0.92). Size was a weak exploratory gate covariate (explore Holm p = 0.049) and failed its registered confirmation test (coefficient +0.23, wrong sign). Predictive claim (confirmed out of sample): the frozen two-type forecaster has an MSE of 0.833 times the pooled AR(1) and 0.831 times the zero forecast on 150 unseen confirmation assets (paired one-sided p = 2.3e-14). Mechanistic claim: the two-type AR(1) structure is supported against i.i.d., one pooled AR, and continuous characteristic loading by evidence that discriminates between these structures (bimodality, half-split persistence r = 0.74 and 0.76, discrete beats continuous by 330 log-lik units per 100 confirmation assets). Why age relates to type is not established.
